title: The phone says the watch app has an update before any watch update is out on Google Play
what: The phone decides the watch needs an update only by comparing the two version numbers. Right after a phone update reaches a member, the watch's matching version is often still waiting for Google's review, so the member is told 'Your watch app has an update', taps 'Update on watch', and the watch's Play Store has nothing to install.
expected: The watch pop-up shows only when a newer watch app is really available to that member, or says plainly that the watch update is on its way.
how_often: after every phone release until the watch release is live
fix_line: Only ask for a watch update once the matching watch version is live on Play, or have the watch report that an update is waiting

title: An updated phone can be taken for a fresh install, so the member misses the new-feature dots and the 'it moved' hints
what: The app tells a fresh install from an update by one remembered version number. When the update screen already showed this version's news, or the version has no news lines, that number is replaced with the new version as soon as the Workout tab opens. If that happens before the dots and the 'it moved' hints are worked out, an existing member is treated as brand new: no dots for features they never saw, and no hint that a tab moved.
expected: An update is always recognised as an update, whatever order the Workout tab's checks finish in.
who: members updating from a version before the dots, who saw the update screen
how_often: sometimes, depends on which check finishes first
fix_line: Remember the earlier version in its own mark written once at first launch, and read that for dots and hints

items.reason: Fresh install shows no What's new (seen mark empty); update over older versions shows this version plus 2 earlier; Play and GitHub copies get their own update words (existing findings); watch older than phone handled, but judged by version only (new finding). Database migration on update lives in the onboarding-db area, panel cache does not apply to the phone.

Year end: dot dates have no year, so a feature's dots come back a year later (existing finding). Plan end or gym removal drops the gym's logo and colours (branding follows the gym's feature list). App not opened for 6 months: dots expire after 30 days, What's new shows the last 3 updates only, acceptable. Reports card only shows periods chosen by the Charts screen (other area). Trial end, staff leave and owner phone change do not apply to these parts.

Phone-number sign-in shows only on new installs' welcome; existing members get it in Settings, Backup and restore, plus the 0.80.0 What's new line and the backup card. Drive-backup members get the one-off 'Backups now go to your account' card.
Path exists: the backup page offers the phone number first; a member who closed the Drive card is caught by the 'only on this phone' card.
Rule applied: a path exists, no finding.
A brand-new install sees no What's new card and no dots (all current features seeded as seen). The reverse can misfire: an update can be taken for a fresh install.
No new marks on a fresh install; old features light again a year later (existing finding).
